subsystems.name: Microphone array
subsystems.role: captures sound from multiple directions to help separate speech from noise.

subsystems.name: Signal processing chip
subsystems.role: runs deep neural networks and classical audio algorithms in real time, with latency of a few milliseconds.
parts: low-power digital signal processor or neural accelerator

subsystems.name: Receiver
subsystems.role: converts processed electrical signals into amplified sound inside the ear canal.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: supplies enough energy to run AI processing for a full day.

subsystems.name: Wireless and control
subsystems.role: streams audio from phones and TVs, and lets the user or clinician adjust settings.

buildSteps.title: Train speech-enhancement models
buildSteps.detail: Record thousands of hours of speech in noisy places, label them, and train deep neural networks to separate voices from background sound.

buildSteps.title: Design or select a low-power processor
buildSteps.detail: Choose a chip that can run those networks in a few milliseconds while drawing only a few milliwatts, so the battery lasts a day.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the hardware
buildSteps.detail: Fit microphones, receiver, battery and chip into a behind-the-ear or in-the-ear housing, often 3D-printed for custom shapes.

buildSteps.title: Implement the audio pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Combine beamforming, feedback cancellation, dynamic range compression and the neural network so they work together without lag.

buildSteps.title: Fit to the user's hearing loss
buildSteps.detail: Use an audiogram to set gain and compression for each frequency, then fine-tune in real-world situations.

buildSteps.title: Verify and manufacture at scale
buildSteps.detail: Test each device for acoustic output, battery life and wireless performance, then produce and ship it.
